expectations.text: Rejects publishing a fixed public Enterprise number: self-serve tiers publish exact numbers, the top tier publishes a process
expectations.evidence: 'Don't publish... The top tier publishes a process, not numbers.'

expectations.text: Keys overrides to the authenticated principal (API key, org, or app installation), never to a person, rejecting attachment to the admin's user account
expectations.evidence: 'Org ID: Always the organization. Never a user ID or email.'

expectations.text: Replaces ad-hoc account-executive discretion with a named, documented override mechanism, since a contact-sales path with no process is the gap
expectations.evidence: 'Written request, named approver, limit register.'

expectations.text: Presents the named override shapes (ticket-based with lead time, spend-based auto-promotion, plan-gated, time-boxed self-serve burst) and picks one deliberately
expectations.evidence: Only the ticket-based flow is given. Spend-based auto-promotion, plan-gated and self-serve burst shapes are not presented or compared.

expectations.text: Specifies a lead time for increase requests, citing vendor precedent such as at least 6 weeks for large increases or 24-hour-minimum structured tickets
expectations.evidence: '≥ 6 weeks, the Stripe-style planning floor for large increases.'

expectations.text: Requires the increase request to carry structured fields such as the key or org, requested rate, and dates or duration
expectations.evidence: 'Organization ID, the API keys... the target limit... start date, and whether... temporary or permanent.'

expectations.text: States explicitly in the docs whether a higher-priced plan implies higher limits, citing the precedent where an Enterprise plan does not raise limits until they are explicitly activated
expectations.evidence: 'The Enterprise plan does not change API limits by itself'; 'this is the OpenAI-style gap'.

expectations.text: Names at least one limit dimension that no override touches, and says so in the policy
expectations.evidence: 'Per-endpoint-class limits... and the concurrency cap are set separately. A higher request quota does not raise them.'

expectations.text: Reserves in writing the right to lower any granted override for platform stability
expectations.evidence: 'We may lower a grant to protect platform stability.'

expectations.text: Requires every granted override to be recorded and keyed somewhere auditable, since an override granted verbally, keyed to nothing, documented nowhere is a named failure mode
expectations.evidence: 'Limit register (source of truth, one row per grant)'.

expectations.text: Routes overrides through support, sales, or an account manager rather than a dashboard toggle, noting the time-boxed self-serve burst as the rare exception
expectations.evidence: 'The AE or customer files the request via a support ticket or form'; platform engineering applies the grant.

expectations.text: Flags persistent override-request volume per quarter as the signal that the published tiers are set too low
expectations.evidence: 'If override requests keep coming each quarter, Pro is set too low.'
